 Oral Order

. 
2. The instant writ petition has been filed by the petitioner under section 226 of the Constitution of India invoking writ jurisdiction of this Court for a direction upon the respondents to make adequate compensation amount in respect of the petitioners' land which has been acquired for the construction of Araria Galgal new B.G. Rail line.

2. After having heard both the sides and on perusal the relevant materials, this Court finds that the petitioner has directly approached this court for invoking writ jurisdiction without availing the statutory remedy available to him under Patna High Court CWJC No.17607 of 2021(3)
dt.04-09-2025 section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, hence, the instant writ petition stands disposed of with giving a liberty to the petitioner to file an application before the Collector-cum-District Magistrate,
Kishanganj (Respondent No.
Shahin Amin vs The State Of Bihar on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189370658/
1 2), for the aforesaid purpose in the next three weeks and if he avails this liberty then the Respondent No.2 shall proceed with his application in the light of the provisions of section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
4. Accordingly, this writ petition stands disposed of.
(Shailendra Singh, J) BKS/-
